definitions.explanation: seeing something incorrectly or mistaking one thing for another

examples.japanese: {見|み}{間違|まちが}いかと{思|おも}った。
examples.english: I thought I was seeing things.

examples.japanese: それは{見|み}{間違|まちが}いじゃないですか。
examples.english: Isn't that just your eyes playing tricks?

examples.japanese: {暗|くら}くて{人|ひと}を{見|み}{間違|まちが}いして{違|ちが}う{人|ひと}に{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: It was dark, and I mistook someone for another person and called out to the wrong person.

notes:
COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{見|み}{間違|まちが}い combines {見|み}る (to see) + {間違|まちが}い (mistake). Note that unlike other ～{間違|まちが}い compounds, this one doesn't have the connecting い.

COMMON CONTEXTS:
- {人違|ひとちが}い - mistaking someone for another person
- {暗|くら}い{場所|ばしょ} - dark places
- {遠|とお}く - from a distance
- {似|に}ている{物|もの} - similar-looking things

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {見|み}{間違|まちが}える (verb) - to mistake (visually)
- {目|め}の{錯覚|さっかく} - optical illusion
- {人違|ひとちが}い - mistaking someone's identity

RELATED ～{間違|まちが}い WORDS:
- {聞|き}き{間違|まちが}い - mishearing
- {言|い}い{間違|まちが}い - slip of the tongue
- {読|よ}み{間違|まちが}い - misreading
